messages:
sophie: Customer (acme-inc) opened an escalation — after switching to PrivateLink they see intermittent 502/503 from the hosted API. Started ~2h after cutover. They provided sample request ids: req_7f1e, req_7f2a. Any obvious quick checks?

raj: Do we know if they used an Interface VPCE to our service (com.amazonaws.vpce-svc-...) or an NLB in their account? Cross-account acceptance done?

sophie: They created an interface endpoint in their account pointing to our service name, we accepted. Endpoint policy looks open (allow *). They enabled private DNS. The interface shows Available but the NLB target group shows multiple targets UNHEALTHY.

miguel: UNHEALTHY targets -> 502s. Common culprits: security group on our targets blocking health check source IPs, target type mismatch (IP vs instance), or private DNS resolving to wrong IP (split-horizon). Also TLS SNI mismatch can make backends reject traffic.

raj: For cross-account PrivateLink the NLB health checks originate from the service side (our account). Confirm the NLB target group's configured port and path. If the target is IP-based, ensure source/dest checks and SG allow the NLB nodes.

sophie: Customer sent NLB health check screenshot: path /health, 443, 200 expected — shows Failed for most targets. They also saw TLS alert "unknown ca" on some handshakes in our edge logs.

miguel: "unknown ca" -> TLS termination mismatch. Two scenarios: (1) Private DNS resolves their hostname to the interface endpoint IP and they are curling using the internal hostname but SNI still needs to match the cert on our NLB. (2) If they are using a custom hostname -> need to add cert on our side or use passthrough. Ask them to curl with SNI to reproduce.

sophie: Asked customer to run:```curl -v --resolve api.redwood.internal:443:10.0.5.12 https://api.redwood.internal/health``` and paste output. Also asked for tcpdump of the handshake from an instance in their VPC.

jen: I can run that. Quick update: we also have a Route53 private hosted zone for redwood.internal in our VPC — could that be overriding the endpoint DNS?

raj: Yes private hosted zones can shadow AWS-provided private DNS for the VPCE. If they have a zone that resolves the API to a private IP that isn't the interface ENI, traffic might be going somewhere else. Check that the A record for the host resolves to the interface endpoint IPs in their subnet.

miguel: Another thing: NLB health checks use the NLB node IPs as source. Ensure the security group on targets allows health checks from the NLB node CIDR (or the health-check SG we use). If the target rejects health checks, ALB/NLB will mark unhealthy and start returning 502/503.

sophie: Customer ran the curl — TLS handshake fails with `SSL: certificate subject did not match SNI`. They confirmed Private DNS was enabled and resolves to the VPCE ENI IPs.

raj: Ok that's SNI mismatch. Two remediation paths: (A) Have client present the SNI matching our cert (api.redwood.com) when calling the endpoint, or (B) add the customer's hostname as an additional SAN on our cert / configure their custom hostname on the endpoint (requires ent config). For quick debug, they can `curl -H "Host: api.redwood.com" --resolve api.redwood.internal:443:10.0.5.12 https://api.redwood.internal/health` to test.

jen: I tried the Host override and curl returns 200 consistently now. Health checks still show unhealthy in the console though — maybe NLB health checks originate without Host header?

miguel: Exactly — NLB health checks use the host header configured in the target group health check. Make sure the TG health check sets Host: api.redwood.com (or uses HTTPS health check with correct SNI) and that the health check path matches. If the TG health check is plain IP-based without correct SNI/Host, backend will reject.

sophie: Action items for customer: 1) Update target group health check to send Host: api.redwood.com (or use IP health check that accepts no SNI) 2) Temporarily allow health check sources in SG so we can verify 3) If they want to use a custom hostname for PrivateLink, open a ticket with product for SAN config.

jen: I'll update TG health check and add a short-lived SG rule to allow from the NLB nodes. I'll post results here.

aws-bot: Incident ticket created: #INC-2026-8421 linked to customer acme-inc. Assigned to eng-sre.

sophie: Thanks — escalated to eng-sre with the curl output and PCAP request. Will follow up after TG change. :thumbsup:
